thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Nasdaq Futures Climb, Led Higher By Apple's Jump

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Nasdaq Futures Climb, Led Higher By Apple's Jump
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Futures for the Dow industrials, S&P 500 show little change
Futures for the Nasdaq-100 index gained ground early Wednesday, boosted by Apple Inc.'s earnings-driven jump in premarket trading.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 looked set for muted moves, however, as traders braced for a Federal Reserve policy statement, as well as ADP's monthly report on private-sector employment.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Nasdaq-100 futures rose by 13 points, or 0.2%, to 6,704.75, trimming sharper gains.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded roughly flat at 24,075, while S&P 500 futures slipped 1.25 points, or less than 0.1%, to 2,651,75, giving up earlier gains.
On Tuesday, the Dow finished 0.3% lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-street-stocks-ready-to-slip-further-with-pfizer-earnings-ahead-2018-05-01), while the S&P 500 advanced by 0.3% and the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite rose 0.9%.
The Dow and S&P are down 2.5% and 0.7% for the year, as of Tuesday's close. The Nasdaq Composite has climbed 3.3%.
What's driving markets?
Apple's stock (AAPL)rose 3.4% in premarket action after the largest American company by market capitalization late Tuesday posted better-than-anticipated earnings and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-rises-after-iphone-sales-fall-short-but-earnings-beat-2018-05-01) for the first quarter.
Check out:Apple earnings were saved by the company's new MVP (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-were-saved-by-the-companys-new-mvp-2018-05-01)
And see: The surprise in Apple earnings -- big growth in China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-surprise-in-apple-earnings-big-growth-in-china-2018-05-01)
Encouraging first-quarter earnings from many companies have helped the main equity benchmarks rally in recent weeks, though investors also have been worried about protectionism and other geopolitical flare-ups.
Which economic releases are on tap?
Fed officials are due to wrap up a two-day meeting, and the policy makers are expected to leave interest rates on hold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/as-market-churns-fed-will-say-it-has-inflation-situation-under-control-2018-04-26). Market participants are watching for any change to plans for a tightening path of two more rate increases in 2018.
The Federal Open Market Committee's policy statement is slated to hit at 2 p.m. Eastern Time.
Don't miss: Why the Fed could make 4 rate hikes this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-will-make-4-rate-hikes-this-year-economists-say-after-latest-gdp-eci-reports-2018-04-27)
ADP's April release on private-sector employment is expected to arrive at 8:15 a.m. Eastern. It typically serves as a preview to Friday's more closely watched jobs report from the U.S. government, also known as the monthly nonfarm payrolls data.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
Which stocks are in focus?
Earnings season continues, with Humana Inc. (HUM) , Clorox Co. (CLX) , Estee Lauder Cos. (EL) and CVS Health Corp. (CVS) expected to release quarterly results ahead of the bell. Also on the early docket are Yum Brands Inc. (YUM) , Molson Coors Brewing Co. (TAP) and Mastercard Inc. (MA)
After the market closes, earnings releases should come from Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) and Tesla Inc. (TSLA) , among others.
